payload.text: A COMMENT CAN DISARM THE CHECKER AND THE CHECKER STILL EXITS 0. shellcheck reads `# shellcheck ` as DIRECTIVE syntax, so a sentence that opens that way is a parse error (SC1072/SC1073) and it answers by SKIPPING the rest of that script's checks. Found by vc in Intent's tests.yml, where the sentence began `# shellcheck IS AN ARMED TOOL FOR THIS PROJECT` -- silent since it was written, in the one project that arms shellcheck as a critic. Devbin's own tree is clean of it, which I checked rather than assumed on 2026-09-22: every `# shellcheck` line here carries one of the six real directive keys. The general shape is the one to carry: a tool whose OWN configuration surface accepts prose will take a comment as configuration, and disarming is not a failure it reports.
